After simplify(), the self-loop and the duplicate edge are gone, shown dashed, leaving a simple four-node cycle." width="100%"} A simple graph has no self-loops (edges from a node to itself) and no multi-edges (multiple edges between the same pair of nodes). This method removes both types, which is a common preprocessing step for algorithms that require simple graphs. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} `simplify()` is exactly `remove_selfloops()` followed by `remove_duplicate_edges()` rolled into one call: self-loops disappear and each group of parallel edges collapses to its earliest survivor (lowest edge ID). Directedness affects only the second step, since $(u, v)$ and $(v, u)$ are distinct pairs in a directed graph but the same pair when undirected. Once it returns, `is_simple()` is guaranteed to be `True`, which is the condition many algorithms in the library quietly assume. ## Examples {.doc-examples} `simplify()` combines `remove_selfloops()` and `remove_duplicate_edges()` in one call. This graph starts with a duplicate "A"-"B" edge and two self-loops, so it isn't simple: ::: {#89cd8a7b .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B"]) .add_edges( [ ("A", "B", 1.0), ("A", "B", 2.0), # duplicate ("A", "A"), # self-loop ("B", "B"), # self-loop ] ) ) g.count_edges(), g.is_simple() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (4, False) ``` ::: ::: After simplifying, only the single genuine "A"-"B" edge remains, and `is_simple()` confirms it: ::: {#d1f45cdc .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} g = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B"]) .add_edges([("A", "B", 1.0), ("A", "B", 2.0), ("A", "A"), ("B", "B")]) .simplify() ) g.count_edges(), g.is_simple() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (1, True) ``` ::: ::: This makes `simplify()` a convenient one-line preprocessing step whenever an algorithm requires a simple graph: ::: {#bb3e1469 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} g = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["X", "Y", "Z"]) .add_edges( [ ("X", "Y"), ("X", "Y"), # duplicate ("Y", "Z"), ("Z", "Z"), # self-loop ] ) .simplify() ) g.is_simple() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` True ``` ::: :::
